dependencies: core Lean 4 only (no mathlib, no Batteries, no external imports)
gate_reuse: Checked by the existing, unmodified papers/data/lean/verify_wayfinder_axioms.py, invoked with --axioms <captured kernel output> --manifest papers/data/lean/flow-scope.json, and by the unmodified check_forbidden_tokens.py, check_lean_axioms.py (enumerate mode, --require-coverage) and leanchecker --fresh replay. No existing gate, test, or recorded negative was changed or relaxed to admit this file.
axiom_policy: Every declaration listed in `theorems` must appear in the `#print axioms` output of the pinned kernel run. Its reported axiom set must be a subset of `permitted_axioms` (the three core Lean assumptions). Any other axiom, and in particular `sorryAx`, fails the gate. A missing declaration fails the gate. The gate parses the kernel's printed output; it does not grep source comments.
code_convention: St lists eight working and six terminal task states. tableStep is the orchestrator transition table (spec section 4); step adds close-to-any-terminal from working states and no successor from terminal states. rank orders working states 8..1 with terminals at 0; backEdge lists the five table edges that do not lower rank. potential b s = 9*b + rank s. lindley q a s = (q + a) - s with truncated subtraction.

theorems.name: FlowBounds.terminal_absorbing
theorems.statement: isTerminal a -> step a b = false
theorems.runtime_predicate: no transition leaves a terminal state

theorems.name: FlowBounds.no_dead_state
theorems.statement: not isTerminal a -> exists b, tableStep a b
theorems.runtime_predicate: every working state has a table successor

theorems.name: FlowBounds.rank_le
theorems.runtime_predicate: ranks lie in 0..8, so one back edge raises rank by at most 8

theorems.name: FlowBounds.rank_or_back_edge
theorems.statement: step a b -> rank b < rank a or backEdge a b
theorems.runtime_predicate: every edge lowers RANK or is in BACK_EDGES

theorems.name: FlowBounds.back_edge_is_table_edge
theorems.statement: backEdge a b -> tableStep a b
theorems.runtime_predicate: each listed back edge is a table edge

theorems.name: FlowBounds.potential_decreases
theorems.statement: stepB b a b' c -> potential b' c < potential b a
theorems.runtime_predicate: 9*budget + rank strictly decreases on every step

theorems.name: FlowBounds.run_length_le
theorems.statement: Run b s n -> n <= 9*b + rank s
theorems.runtime_predicate: remaining steps are bounded by RANK_SPAN*budget + rank

theorems.name: FlowBounds.run_length_no_budget
theorems.runtime_predicate: with no back edges a run has at most 8 steps

theorems.name: FlowBounds.occupancy_conserved
theorems.statement: working l + finished l = length l

theorems.name: FlowBounds.move_preserves_total
theorems.statement: length (set l i s) = length l
theorems.runtime_predicate: moving one task preserves the total

theorems.name: FlowBounds.occupancy_conserved_under_move
theorems.statement: working (set l i s) + finished (set l i s) = length l

theorems.name: FlowBounds.lindley_le_of_arrivals_le
theorems.statement: a <= s -> lindley q a s <= q
theorems.runtime_predicate: backlog does not grow when arrivals <= capacity

theorems.name: FlowBounds.lindley_surplus
theorems.statement: s <= a -> lindley q a s = q + (a - s)
theorems.runtime_predicate: backlog grows by exactly the surplus

theorems.name: FlowBounds.lindley_mono
theorems.statement: q <= q' -> lindley q a s <= lindley q' a s

theorems.name: FlowBounds.lindley_conservation
theorems.statement: lindley q a s + min (q + a) s = q + a
theorems.runtime_predicate: carried-over plus served equals work present

theorems.name: FlowBounds.backlog_le_start
theorems.statement: (all buckets a <= s) -> backlog q l <= q
theorems.runtime_predicate: keeping_up / draining never end above the start

theorems.name: FlowBounds.backlog_growth
theorems.statement: (all buckets s + d <= a) -> q + d*length l <= backlog q l
theorems.runtime_predicate: growing backlogs gain at least the net rate per bucket

runtime_verified_not_lean_proved.detail: That the deployed VALID_TRANSITIONS table equals tableStep. Checked at runtime by jev-flow checkLifecycleModel (selftest FL1, FL2) and reported in every snapshot as lifecycle_model.
That each task is allowed only finitely many re-gate / re-decide loops. The bound is conditional on the budget; the worker's retry and continuation caps supply it.
That scheduled sweeps fire and that an operator eventually acts on work the instrument marks as waiting on the operator. No fairness or liveness statement is proved.
Arrival, completion and backlog counts come from D1 rows over a trailing window; they are measurements, not theorems.

nonclaims: No new mathematics: workflow-net soundness (van der Aalst 1997), ranking-function termination and the Lindley recursion (1952) are prior art; the file pins the deployed table.
No liveness under fairness: the run bound limits length, it does not show a waiting task is ever moved.
No statement about concurrency, CAS claims, leases or D1 transactions.
No queueing-theoretic stationarity, stability or Little's-law claim; the backlog identities are per-bucket arithmetic.
No statement about model outputs, policy gates or approval correctness.
The holder classification (system / operator) of the instrument is a runtime rule and is not formalized here.

statement_pinning.pin: sha256 of the normalized Lean statement text
statement_pinning.normalization: Lean comments stripped (/- -/ nested blocks, -- line); string literals respected; statement = source text between the declaration name and the first top-level ':=' (or the first top-level match-arm '|' line for pattern proofs); whitespace runs collapsed to single spaces; proof text excluded.
statement_pinning.policy: A pin mismatch fails CI. A legitimate statement change requires a deliberate pin regeneration in the same PR, with the statement diff reviewed as a semantic change. Do NOT regenerate pins to make CI pass without reviewing the statement diff.

definitions.pin: sha256 over the sorted 'command-key:normalized-text' entries of EVERY top-level command in the lean_file -- imports, open/namespace/end wrappers, attribute lines (hashed WITH the declaration they decorate), declarations of any kind, set_option lines, #print/#eval/#check, notation/syntax/macro/elab, run_cmd blocks (comments stripped, whitespace collapsed). theorem/lemma/example proof bodies are EXCLUDED: the hashed text is the statement through the first top-level ':=' (inclusive) or up to the first match-arm line. 'decls' maps each command key (<kind>:<name>, or <kind> with #N collision suffixes for unnamed commands) to its own normalized-text sha256
definitions.policy: A commands-hash mismatch FAILS CI even when every theorem statement is unchanged: adding ANY top-level command (including an attribute-prefixed declaration, which round 2's line-start keyword regex missed), redefining a definition, or adding a set_option/#print/notation line changes what the pinned theorems actually prove or how the file elaborates, so a legitimate change requires a deliberate definitions-block regeneration IN THE SAME PR, with the command diff reviewed as a semantic change. Do NOT regenerate the block to make CI pass without reviewing the diff. Proof-body-only rewrites (kernel-checked content) do NOT change the hash and need no regeneration. A block pinning zero commands is refused (vacuous pin), and a block whose schema is not commands-v2 FAILS the gate (fail-closed; an old definition-pins/1 defs-only block cannot be verified against command hashing).
